findings: The reason for DEC-19. By hand, not formalized (no E_0 in the library): in E_0 minus a point w of the BTZ line below p, with z on that line below w, z << p_n for regular p_n -> p with p ∉ J^-(p_n) (a chronal curve from a BTZ point leaves the line at once and avoids w), while J^-(p) = ]w,p]; so lem:cup_cap_BTZ as printed (strongly causal) fails for this strongly causal singular flat spacetime, granted that E_0 is strongly causal and p ∈ Int J^+(z) (the fact the proof of prop:K_calcul (c) uses). Its only use (l.2122) is in a globally hyperbolic setting, where it holds. The proof 'as for lem:J_int' (l.1831) does not reduce to a chart: z may lie outside it. Under DEC-19 the lemma is stated for globally hyperbolic M and its certificate is cupCapBTZAsPrinted_of_globallyHyperbolic; the printed strongly causal form stays the Prop Causal.Causality.CupCapBTZAsPrinted, not asserted, with this finding. findings: The reason for DEC-18. As printed (no strong causality), the remark overclaims: theo:geroch asks local causal convexity and a pair of admissible measures, and prop:mesure_admissible gives the measures only for strongly causal M; nothing in Section 3 makes a singular flat spacetime strongly causal (l.1216 reads 'locally causally convex => strongly causal'). By hand, not formalized (no E_alpha in the library): for alpha > 0, E_alpha modulo a translation along its timelike singular line is a connected singular flat spacetime with a non-empty singular locus (so the example does not depend on whether A = R_+ allows an empty one); its singular line closes into a closed timelike curve, it is totally vicious (J^-(q) = M for every q), and it carries no measure admissible in the past (property 3 fails). E^{1,2} modulo a timelike translation is the same example if an empty singular locus is allowed. None of (i)-(iii) holds there, so theo:geroch_sing without strong causality is not refuted, but its proof (l.1781-1785) needs strong causality for (ii)=>(iii) and (iii)=>(i). The example is local (not a kb/0014 artefact). Since line/massive_line ask the closed embedding only when M is causal, the structure does not exclude such a quotient. Under DEC-18 the remark and theo:geroch_sing assume M strongly causal.
J^±(p) ≠ {p} (l.1783-1785) follows abstractly: I^±(p) is non-empty and open (or J^-(p) accumulates at p at a BTZ point) and M has no isolated point; the '3-dimensional J^+(p)' is not needed.

SCOPE: VecteurFlow.isOpenMap is the half of the homeomorphism the paper asserts rather than argues (l.1792), so the formal content of geroch_sing_split is the bijectivity argument (orbits meet the Cauchy surface exactly once, and are injective). geroch_sing_split is sorry-free, asks IsCausal (DEC-18 gives strong causality, hence causality) and does not use the structure; witnessed on the timelike line (timelikeLine_vecteurFlow). Without VecteurFlow, the abstract statement would be stronger than the paper's (which claims the splitting for manifolds only) and of unknown truth: the l.1309-1314 counterexample is non-Hausdorff, excluded by t2, and a Hausdorff Y-tree is not tarentin at its branch point.

findings: l.1329-1331 (the sentence before the definition; the audit cited l.1327) give E_0 the metric −dτ² + dρ² + ρ²dθ² and call its singular locus {ρ = 0} a lightlike line. With that metric ∂_τ has norm −1 on {ρ = 0}, so the line is timelike, contradicting 'lightlike' (and defi:causal_E0's I^-(p) = ∅). Most likely a transcription error: the flat extreme-BTZ metric has the form −2 dτ dρ + ρ² dθ², for which {ρ = 0} is lightlike. (Auditor's side observation, by hand; nothing in WP-11 depends on the metric.)

The sentence I^+(p) = J^+(p) \ sing_0 (l.1352-1355) is flagged in the source at l.1351 as quoted from the thesis where it is asserted without proof; WP-11's field Iplus_eq assumes it, globally, and lt_of_le_of_not_mem, K_monotone, K_densite_sing, K_ordre and mesure_admissible rest on it.
questions: Is the E_0 metric of l.1330 meant to be −2dτdρ + ρ²dθ² (lightlike singular line)?

kb_proposals: Singular-part statements take h : C.SingularFlatAxioms sing (CausalScaffold.SingularFlat): h.K_calcul, h.K_monotone, h.mem_sing_zero_of_le (J^- of a BTZ point is BTZ), h.isClosed_Jminus, h.lt_of_le_of_not_mem are ready; typeclass fields are used with haveI := h.t2 / h.secondCountable (first countability then by instance).

Under push-up with Z^+ = M and Z^- ⊇ reg, density J^± ⊆ closure K^± is immediate given I^+ = J^+ \ sing_0 globally at BTZ points (K_densite_sing); the global form is itself the chart + arc-connectedness step of the paper.

A non-empty sing_0 is witnessed on neither the timelike nor the lightlike line (timelikeLine_sing_zero, lightlikeLine_not_mem_Zplus; no general dimension bound is proved): witness BTZAxioms alone on the lightlike line with sing_0 = ℝ, and say the full structure with sing_0 ≠ ∅ has no witness.

liminf-of-pasts statements (lem:cup_cap, lem:cup_cap_BTZ) need closed J^+; strong causality does not give it — ask GH (or closed J^+) and say so. A printed statement believed false is a Prop definition (CupCapBTZAsPrinted), never a sorry'd theorem.

A differentiable object a proof uses (a flow, lem:vecteur) can be a data-carrying named hypothesis with exactly the C⁰ properties the proof asserts (VecteurFlow: open ψ, inextensible orbits, injective on causal M), witnessed on the timelike line by x + t; say which of those properties the paper asserts without argument (here the openness of ψ, l.1792).

When the author rules that a statement assumes a hypothesis (DEC-18, DEC-19), the strengthened-form theorem becomes the principal declaration, the hypothesis row reads 'carried', and the printed form survives only as a Prop with its finding; delete any sorry'd bridge to the printed form.
